net-01-c3.text: D. Waitzman (BBN STC) (1990). A Standard for the Transmission of IP Datagrams on Avian Carriers (RFC 1149). IETF Datatracker / RFC Editor.
net-01-c3.quote: The scroll of paper is wrapped around one leg of the avian carrier.

net-02-c1.text: (2011). Free Pool of IPv4 Address Space Depleted. The Number Resource Organization.
net-02-c1.quote: Montevideo, 3 February 2011 – The Number Resource Organization (NRO) announced today that the free pool of available IPv4 addresses is now fully depleted.
net-02-c1.claim: That's 4.3 billion addresses: generous in 1980, exhausted by 2011.

net-02-c1.text: S. Deering, R. Hinden (2017). RFC 8200: Internet Protocol, Version 6 (IPv6) Specification. RFC Editor (IETF).
net-02-c1.quote: IPv6 increases the IP address size from 32 bits to 128 bits, to support more levels of addressing hierarchy, a much greater number of addressable nodes, and simpler autoconfiguration of addresses.
net-02-c1.claim: IPv6 uses 128 bits, written as eight groups of four hex digits (e.g., 2001:0db8::1).

net-02-c3.text: Root Servers. Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA).
net-02-c3.quote: The authoritative name servers that serve the DNS root zone, often known simply as the “root servers”, are a network of hundreds of servers in many countries around the world. They are configured in the DNS root zone as 13 named authorities, as follows.
net-02-c3.claim: Root servers (13 logical servers, replicated worldwide) know where the top-level domain servers are.

net-03-c1.text: Wesley M. Eddy (2022). RFC 9293: Transmission Control Protocol (TCP). RFC Editor (IETF).
net-03-c1.quote: The "three-way handshake" is the procedure used to establish a connection.
net-03-c1.claim: TCP starts with a three-way handshake: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK.

net-03-c1.text: Lisong Xu, Sangtae Ha, Injong Rhee, Vidhi Goel, Lars Eggert (2023). RFC 9438: CUBIC for Fast and Long-Distance Networks. RFC Editor (IETF).
net-03-c1.quote: CUBIC has been adopted as the default TCP congestion control algorithm in the Linux, Windows, and Apple stacks, and has been used and deployed globally.
net-03-c1.claim: Algorithms like CUBIC (default in Linux) and BBR (Google's, used in YouTube) determine how quickly senders can ramp up.

net-03-c2.text: Evolution of HTTP. MDN Web Docs.
net-03-c2.quote: QUIC runs multiple streams over UDP and implements packet loss detection and retransmission independently for each stream, so that if an error occurs, only the stream with data in that packet is blocked.
net-03-c2.claim: QUIC, the foundation of HTTP/3, runs over UDP and reimplements connections, encryption, and retransmission with much lower latency than TCP+TLS.

net-03-c3.text: Evolution of HTTP. MDN Web Docs.
net-03-c3.quote: HTTP/1.1 was first published as RFC 2068 in January 1997.
net-03-c3.claim: HTTP/1.1 (1997) added persistent connections and pipelining.

net-03-c3.text: Evolution of HTTP. MDN Web Docs.
net-03-c3.quote: Officially standardized in May 2015, HTTP/2 use peaked in January 2022 at 46.9% of all websites (see these stats).
net-03-c3.claim: HTTP/2 (2015) introduced binary framing, multiplexed streams over one TCP connection, and header compression.

net-04-c1.quote: The same-origin policy is a critical security mechanism that restricts how a document or script loaded by one origin can interact with a resource from another origin.
net-04-c1.claim: Browsers enforce the same-origin policy: JavaScript on example.com cannot read responses from bank.com.

net-04-c1.text: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS). MDN Web Docs.
net-04-c1.quote: Additionally, for HTTP request methods that can cause side-effects on server data (in particular, HTTP methods other than GET, or POST with certain MIME types), the specification mandates that browsers "preflight" the request, soliciting supported methods from the server with the HTTP OPTIONS request method
net-04-c1.claim: For "non-simple" requests (custom headers, methods other than GET/POST/HEAD, etc.), the browser sends a preflight OPTIONS request first to ask permission.

net-04-c2.text: Karen Scarfone, Paul Hoffman (2009). Guidelines on Firewalls and Firewall Policy (SP 800-41 Rev. 1). National Institute of Standards and Technology.
net-04-c2.quote: Because of the dynamic nature of hosts, networks, protocols, and applications, deny by default is a more secure approach than permitting all traffic that is not explicitly forbidden.
net-04-c2.claim: Firewalls typically follow a default-deny approach: block everything, then explicitly allow what you need.

net-05-c1.text: E. Rescorla (2018). RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3. RFC Editor (IETF).
net-05-c1.quote: Confidentiality: Data sent over the channel after establishment is only visible to the endpoints.
net-05-c1.claim: HTTPS = HTTP over TLS fixes this by adding three guarantees: confidentiality (encrypted), integrity (tamper-detected), authenticity (you really are talking to who you think you are).

net-05-c2.text: (2011). Operation Black Tulip: Certificate authorities lose authority. European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).
net-05-c2.quote: In the attack false certificates were created for hundreds of websites, including Google and Skype.
net-05-c2.claim: Compromised CAs (DigiNotar, 2011) issued fake certs for major domains.

net-05-c3.text: E. Rescorla (2018). RFC 8446: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3. RFC Editor (IETF).
net-05-c3.quote: Static RSA and Diffie-Hellman cipher suites have been removed; all public-key based key exchange mechanisms now provide forward secrecy.
net-05-c3.claim: This property is called forward secrecy, and TLS 1.3 makes it mandatory.

net-05-c3.text: Chad Boutin (2024). NIST Releases First 3 Finalized Post-Quantum Encryption Standards. National Institute of Standards and Technology.
net-05-c3.quote: The standard is based on the CRYSTALS-Kyber algorithm, which has been renamed ML-KEM, short for Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism.
net-05-c3.claim: NIST has standardized lattice-based schemes (Kyber for key exchange, Dilithium for signatures).
